reason: The long UAL / short AAL pair entered 2026-10-26 has stayed market-neutral as designed. Both legs rose with the sector (UAL +3.53%, AAL short -3.28%), so the spread is about flat after one week, and neither stop is near (UAL -10%, AAL short -25%). Research this week used WebSearch and WebFetch, but the October-specific coverage I found was thin and mostly from aggregator sites, so this is not deep confirmation. What I could find supports the divergence. AAL's Q3 (Oct 22) only met EPS estimates, and early October brought at least four sell-side target cuts (Wells Fargo to $14, Goldman, TD Cowen). American also dismissed the United merger idea in April, which removed a speculative tailwind. United executives reported premium revenue up about 6% year over year and record business ticketing in early October, and the consensus is still Strong Buy. Analyses this year repeatedly flag AAL as the more fuel-sensitive and more leveraged carrier with less premium support. A one-week flat spread is noise, not a broken thesis. Rebalancing would cost real basis points, especially on AAL, which trades under $15 and is charged 12bps per side. Keeping 70% in cash at 4% keeps gross exposure modest in a mandate built on one high-conviction relative-value pair. No trade.
